vignette: A 66-year-old woman is brought in with sudden weakness of the right leg, much worse than the arm, with the face spared. She is slow to respond, has a grasp reflex in the right hand and is incontinent of urine. Speech is preserved.

options.text: Left middle cerebral artery, superior division

explanation: Leg-predominant contralateral weakness with abulia, a grasp reflex and incontinence follows infarction of the medial frontal lobe and paracentral lobule, the territory of the anterior cerebral artery, where the leg is represented on the homunculus.
